question.text: Mr. Deepak Iyer, Manager of Vindhya Debt Opportunities (Cat II AIF), wishes to invest in Security Receipts issued by an ARC. Which of the following investments is EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED under the SARFAESI / AIF framework due to conflict of interest?

answer.text: Investing in SRs backed by stressed loans of an unrelated mid-cap textile company
Investing in SRs rated below investment grade by CRISIL
Investing in SRs issued by an ARC that happens to be the fund's portfolio investee company
Investing in SRs denominated in foreign currency

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.1.2 (Distressed Debt Opportunities), an AIF cannot invest in SRs issued by an ARC which is its portfolio investee company, and also cannot invest in SRs backed by underlying loans of its associate or group companies — both are related-party / conflict-of-interest prohibitions. The Trap: Unrelated corporate stressed loans are exactly what SRs are for. Rating below investment grade is a risk factor, not a prohibition. FX denomination is a structural feature, not a conflict issue. Cross-Exam Context: This conflict rule parallels the AIF-related-party framework tested in XIX-A. III-A (Compliance) also covers related-party restrictions across intermediaries. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before subscribing to any SR, run the ARC issuer's shareholding pattern through your portfolio list — and do the same check on the underlying loan pool. Missing this check is a common audit finding in Cat II debt AIFs.
